metadata.title: When Teams Split Work Too Early
metadata.description:
Extra workers can look like progress while hiding the routing problem. The useful test is simpler: split the work only when the boundary changes memory, tools, permissions, or evaluation.

Claim: Splitting work across extra workers is a workaround unless each worker owns a real boundary.

Evidence: Local cinematic captions show the single-worker versus swarm comparison.; The paired research breakdown covers the 53.7 percent token reduction and coordination tax.; The essay argues that decomposition quality beats coordination theater.

Technical dilemma: If one worker can hold the context and tools, what exact boundary justifies the second one?

Author note: I was skeptical of the anti-swarm framing until the cost and latency comparison made the boundary test unavoidable.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/the-illusion-of-the-swarm

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AigaLYfpFZc

metadata.title: Memory Needs an Owner
metadata.description:
Better recall does not fix memory conflict by itself. The practical question is who owns the state when notes, retrieved facts, and current instructions disagree.

Claim: Memory fails when stored facts do not have an authority rule that decides what wins.

Evidence: Local captions frame memory failure as attention and authority loss.; The paired research breakdown distinguishes recall from governed state.; Shorts follow-through isolates authority failure in compact examples.

Technical dilemma: When memory conflicts with the current task, which source should win, and where is that rule stored?

Author note: The useful shift was treating memory as a control surface, not a bigger storage bucket.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-ii-memory-needs

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pj4sjWvyJVQ

metadata.title: The Second Worker Needs a Boundary
metadata.description:
More workers do not automatically add intelligence. They add handoffs. The useful design question is whether the second worker owns a different boundary or only repeats the same context with a new label.

Claim: A second worker earns its place only when it owns a distinct boundary in state, action, or evaluation.

Evidence: Local captions state the boundary test for worker splits.; The paired research breakdown covers handoffs, tools, and evaluation boundaries.; Existing Shorts isolate the coordination tax failure mode.

Technical dilemma: What has to be different before the second worker is design, not theater?

Author note: The rule that survived review was not more roles; it was sharper ownership boundaries.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-iv-the-second-agent

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xxd2VKlqiL4

metadata.title: Fix the Support Before the Model
metadata.description:
Shopping for a stronger model is often the late move. First inspect the task support: decomposition, checks, state, and the handoff between plan and action.

Claim: Many reasoning failures come from weak task support before they come from weak models.

Evidence: Local captions diagnose the support layer before model choice.; The paired research breakdown covers planning and reasoning supports.; The Shorts package isolates the failed-support pattern.

Technical dilemma: When a model fails a task, how do you separate model weakness from broken support?

Author note: The strongest corrective move was to inspect the task support before blaming the model.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-iii-diagnose-the

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LykGDaONozw

metadata.title: The Work Process Is the Product
metadata.description:
Tuning instructions is too narrow. The better object is the whole work process: inputs, checks, evidence, failures, and the rule for deciding what changed.

Claim: Optimization works when the work process becomes the object under test.

Evidence: Local captions frame optimization around the work process itself.; The paired research breakdown connects evaluation loops to production behavior.; Existing Shorts show drift from small instruction changes.

Technical dilemma: What do you measure when the work process, not the model, is the thing changing?

Author note: The useful unit of improvement turned out to be the process, not the sentence-level instruction.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-bonus-the-workflow

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2Fs1iDw5I3Y

metadata.title: Hardware Decides What Ships
metadata.description:
A design can look elegant in a paper and still lose in production. The deciding filter is often hardware fit: memory movement, kernels, availability, cost, and ecosystem lag.

Claim: Hardware friction decides which designs survive deployment pressure.

Evidence: Local captions frame hardware friction as the shipping filter.; The essay maps friction points that block deployment.; Shorts follow-through covers FlashAttention and ecosystem lag.

Technical dilemma: When a design looks better on paper, what hardware friction would make you reject it?

Author note: The decisive evidence was how often elegant designs failed because the hardware path was not ready.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/the-hardware-friction-map

metadata.title: Hardware Filters Progress
metadata.description:
The winning design is not always the cleanest idea. It is the one that can pass through chips, kernels, memory paths, tooling, and deployment economics without collapsing.

Claim: Architecture progress becomes real only after it passes the hardware compatibility filter.

Evidence: Local captions frame compatibility as the deployment filter.; The essay compares designs through hardware constraints.; The Shorts package includes concrete filter examples.

Technical dilemma: What compatibility test should a new design pass before you call it progress?

Author note: The research forced the question away from novelty and toward compatibility.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/what-actually-works-the-hardware

metadata.title: Specs Need a Surface
metadata.description:
Fast code generation creates the wrong kind of speed if intent is only in chat. Reviewable work needs a surface that names decisions, tests, and the rule for changing them.

Claim: Generated code becomes reviewable when controlling intent lives in a maintained specification surface.

Evidence: Local captions connect generated code to maintained specs.; The paired research breakdown covers why specs become source authority.; Visual slide assets expose the specification surface as an inspectable object.

Technical dilemma: If intent lives only in chat, what exactly is a reviewer supposed to verify?

Author note: The key point is not documentation volume; it is where controlling intent is allowed to live.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/the-specification-surface-is-the

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I6gKAyYRfZU
